passage:
"Why are you talking like Karan bhaiya now?" Vinita asked.
"Like what?"
"'Bro, that's literally so basic.' You've said it six times since dinner."
"He's cool, Didi. Everyone in school wants to be around him."
"Fine, he's cool. What did you do at lunch today?"
"I sat at Karan bhaiya's table."
"And Sameer?"
Rafiq paused. "He was sitting alone. I pretended I didn't see."
"Rafiq. Take what you like from Karan, the way he speaks up in class, his football. But don't drop Sameer or leave your own voice behind to get his attention."
"...I know."
"Go sit with Sameer tomorrow."
Rafiq exhaled. "Okay. I'll ask him about the match."

qa.q: What phrase did Vinita say Rafiq had repeated six times since dinner?
Why did Rafiq pretend not to see Sameer sitting alone, and how does Rafiq seem to feel about it?
qa.a: Rafiq wanted to fit in at Karan bhaiya's table and earn his notice, but the pause and "I know" suggest Rafiq feels guilty.

qa.q: What did Vinita advise Rafiq to do about Karan and Sameer?
qa.a: Take what inspires Rafiq from Karan, keep Rafiq's own voice, and not drop the old friend Sameer. Go sit with Sameer tomorrow.

qa.q: How might Sameer have felt seeing Rafiq at Karan bhaiya's table?
qa.a: Probably hurt and left out, since he was sitting alone and Rafiq pretended not to see him.

grounding: The protagonist idolises a popular senior and copies him; an older sibling urges the protagonist to build a voice of their own and keep old friends.

passage:
In the school cultural club, Charu worshipped Rashmi didi from Class 12. Rashmi didi wore silver jhumkas, laughed with her head back, and said "honestly, yaar" every other sentence. By December, Charu had silver jhumkas too, and said "honestly, yaar" so often her mother noticed.
She'd also stopped sitting with Pooja, her friend since Class 3, because Rashmi didi's group sat on the stage steps.
At the rehearsal for the annual play, Rashmi didi said, "Charu, Pooja's writing is so cringe. Tell her to drop out." Charu felt her stomach twist. Pooja had written half the script.
She thought about it all through practice. She loved how Rashmi didi spoke on stage. But not this.
Afterwards, Charu went to find Pooja in the library. "Your script's the best part of this play. And I'm sorry I disappeared."
Pooja looked up. "You sound like Rashmi."
Charu laughed. "Honestly, yaar. I'm working on my own voice."

qa.q: What did Charu start wearing, like Rashmi didi?
How did Charu feel when Rashmi didi asked her to tell Pooja to drop out?
qa.a: She felt her stomach twist; she was torn between admiring Rashmi didi and loyalty to Pooja.

qa.q: What did Charu do, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She refused to hurt Pooja, apologised for disappearing, and began working on her own voice while still learning from Rashmi didi.

qa.q: How might Pooja have felt when Charu stopped sitting with her?
qa.a: Pooja probably felt hurt and left behind by her oldest friend, which is why she teases Charu for sounding like Rashmi.

grounding: A teen who idolises a popular senior and copies her style refuses to drop an old friend or her values and starts building her own voice.

passage:
Dear Pintu,
I owe you an apology, so here it is on paper.
Since September, I've been following Nikita didi from Class 12 around like a shadow. She's head of the football team, everyone listens to her, and I wanted to be just like her. I started talking like her, walking like her, even cut my hair like hers.
And I stopped hanging out with you. When you asked me to come to the science fair, I said I was busy. I was actually waiting outside the football field hoping she'd notice me.
Last week I heard her mocking the Class 8 kids, and I laughed along. Then I felt sick. I don't want to be the kind of person who laughs at kids for her attention.
I still admire how she leads the team. I'll keep that. But the rest I'm dropping.
Science fair's in two weeks. Can I still help with your volcano?
Santosh

qa.q: Who did Santosh follow around since September?
How did Santosh feel after laughing along at the Class 8 kids?
qa.a: Santosh felt sick and ashamed, realising the copying had led to dropping values for her attention.

qa.q: What is Santosh keeping and what is Santosh dropping, and why is that wise?
qa.a: Santosh keeps admiring how she leads the team but drops the copying and mocking, building a personal voice while reconnecting with Pintu.

qa.q: How might Pintu have felt when Santosh kept saying no?
qa.a: Pintu probably felt hurt and forgotten, especially when Santosh skipped the science fair invitation.

grounding: A teen who idolises a popular senior and copies her notices the cost to an old friendship and values and starts building a voice of their own.
